seo.title: Gemini Calls Local Businesses: What to Know
seo.meta_description: Gemini can now call local businesses to book appointments for its users, disclosing it's an AI. What Anaheim and Orange County businesses should prepare.

h1: Gemini Calls Local Businesses: How AI Assistants Now Book Appointments by Phone
answer: Gemini calls local businesses on a user's behalf as part of Tasks in Gemini, announced November 17, 2026. In Google's example, Gemini found two nearby dealerships on Google Maps, called both, booked an appointment and added it to the user's calendar, disclosing to the business that it is an AI. Google says businesses can opt out. Anaheim and Orange County businesses should be ready to handle these calls.
key_takeaways: Gemini can call businesses to book appointments for its users.
Google says Gemini discloses it's an AI.
Businesses can opt out, according to Google.
Accurate Maps details decide who gets called.

sections.heading: What Google announced
sections.body_html: On November 17, 2026, Google introduced an update to Gemini that lets people hand off tasks. Google says it is rolling out free of charge in the U.S., Japan, Korea, Canada, Australia and India, using its Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, with some advanced features starting in the U.S.

sections.heading: The example Google gave
sections.body_html: In Google's post, a user asked Gemini to call the two nearest dealerships to book an early Friday service appointment. Gemini found the nearest shops on Google Maps, called both at once, booked at the shop that accepts appointments, and put the appointment on the user's calendar in under five minutes.

sections.heading: What businesses should know about the calls
sections.body_html: Google says Gemini disclosed right away to the dealership that it is an AI, that businesses can opt out whenever they want, and that Gemini won't share the user's payment or private account information unless the user says so.

sections.heading: Why this matters for local businesses
sections.body_html: Together with Ask Maps finding appointments, this means more customers will reach local businesses through an AI assistant rather than calling themselves. The businesses an assistant chooses to call are found through Google Maps, so the accuracy of your Business Profile now affects whether you get the call at all.

sections.heading: Who it affects first
sections.body_html:
• Auto repair and dealership service departments.
  • Salons, spas and beauty services.
  • Medical and dental offices with phone booking.
  • Home services that schedule visits.
  • Restaurants that take reservations by phone.

sections.heading: Prepare your phone line
sections.body_html: An AI call may be short and specific: a service, a time window and a name. Make sure calls are answered or returned promptly, and that whoever answers can check availability and confirm a booking clearly. A full voicemail box or a long phone tree can lose the appointment to a competitor that answers.

sections.heading: Keep Maps details accurate
sections.body_html: Gemini found the dealerships on Google Maps. Your category, services, hours, phone number and whether you take appointments or walk-ins all help an assistant choose and contact the right business. Check them on your Google Business Profile.

sections.heading: Say how you book
sections.body_html: Gemini booked at the shop that accepts appointments rather than walk-ins only. State clearly on your profile and website whether you take appointments, how far ahead and for which services, so assistants and customers can match you to what they need.

sections.heading: Train staff for AI-assisted calls
sections.body_html: Brief your team that some callers may be AI assistants acting for a customer. Treat them like any caller: confirm the service, time and name, and send any confirmation through your normal process. If a booking needs information only the customer can give, ask for a callback number.

sections.heading: Opting out
sections.body_html: Google says businesses can opt out. Before deciding, consider that customers who use assistants will simply book with a business that accepts the calls. For most local businesses, preparing to handle them is likely the better choice.

sections.heading: A checklist for this month
sections.body_html:
1. Check category, services, hours and phone on your Business Profile.
  2. State whether you take appointments or walk-ins.
  3. Make sure calls are answered or returned quickly.
  4. Brief staff on AI-assisted calls.
  5. Keep your booking link working.

sections.heading: A worked example
sections.body_html: Imagine an auto repair shop in Garden Grove that often misses calls during busy mornings. It sets up call forwarding to a second phone, lists brake, oil and inspection services clearly on its profile, states that it takes appointments, and trains staff to confirm bookings from AI callers the same way as any customer. When a nearby driver asks Gemini to book a service, the shop is ready.

sections.heading: Questions owners ask us
sections.body_html: Owners often ask whether these calls are legitimate. Google says Gemini discloses that it's an AI right away, so staff should hear that at the start. Another common question is whether customers' private details are shared. Google says Gemini won't give out payment or private account information unless the user says so. Owners also ask whether this replaces online booking. No; it adds another way customers reach you, so keep both working.

sections.heading: How this fits with Ask Maps
sections.body_html: Google has also launched Ask Maps features that find appointments and can call local businesses. For Anaheim and Orange County businesses, the message is the same across both: accurate profiles, clear booking information and answered phones decide who gets the business when an assistant does the searching.

sections.heading: Measure the effect
sections.body_html: Ask new customers how they found you and whether an assistant booked for them, and track missed calls. If missed calls are high, fixing call handling may bring more bookings than any marketing change.

sections.heading: Keep your website consistent
sections.body_html: Assistants also read your website. Make sure it lists the same services, hours, phone number and booking options as your Business Profile, so any assistant sees one clear answer wherever it looks.

sections.heading: Handling busy times
sections.body_html: The calls that matter most often arrive when you are busiest, such as Monday mornings for auto shops or Friday afternoons for salons. If you can't answer every call live, set up a call-back routine: a short voicemail that says when you'll return calls, a person responsible for returning them within the hour, and a simple log so no booking request is lost. Some businesses use a call-answering service during peak hours, given a clear list of services, availability and booking rules. Whatever you choose, test it by calling your own number at a busy time and seeing what a customer, or an assistant, would experience.

sections.heading: What to put on your Business Profile
sections.body_html: Use the profile fields Google provides as fully as possible: the most specific primary category, additional categories that genuinely apply, every service you offer with a short description, accurate hours including holidays, and an appointment or booking link if you have one. In the description, say plainly whether you take appointments, walk-ins or both, and for which services. An assistant choosing between nearby businesses can only use what it can read, so complete, accurate fields make it easier to choose you.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: Gemini can now call local businesses to book appointments for its users, disclosing that it's an AI. Anaheim and Orange County businesses should keep Maps details accurate, state how they book, answer calls promptly and brief staff, so assistants choose and reach them.

faqs.q: Can Gemini call businesses for people?
faqs.a: Yes. Google's November 17, 2026 post describes Gemini calling dealerships to book an appointment.

faqs.q: Does Gemini say it's an AI?
faqs.a: Google says it disclosed right away that it is an AI.
Google says businesses can opt out whenever they want.

faqs.q: How does Gemini find businesses to call?
faqs.a: In Google's example, it found the nearest shops on Google Maps.

faqs.q: Does Gemini share customers' payment details?
faqs.a: Google says not unless the user says so.
Check Maps details, state booking options and make sure calls are answered.
